identity.name: TrackMan Intelligence
identity.goal: Drive fitting bookings and coaching sessions

visualDirection.mood: Clinical precision. Data权威. TrackMan blue dominance.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: TrackMan data is the hero. Numbers, charts, launch monitor visuals. Chrome golf clubs on dark backgrounds. PGA Tour stat comparisons. Clean, scientific, premium. Think golf analytics lab meets luxury sports brand.
imageReferences: TrackMan launch monitor screen with ball flight data
Chrome iron head with data overlay (TrackMan numbers)
Golfer swing capture with split-screen stat comparison
Dark background, premium equipment photography
visualDirection.colorUsage: Use TrackMan blue (#0066CC) as dominant brand colour. Green (#00CC77) for positive metrics and CTAs. Gold for pricing. Never use for backgrounds — text only. Keep dark backgrounds consistent.
visualDirection.typography: Roboto Condensed Bold for numbers and headlines. Inter for body. Monospace for data labels.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split screen: product/club on left, TrackMan data overlay on right. Dark backgrounds throughout. Numbers should dominate the visual hierarchy.
contentExamples: Your drive: 217m. PGA Tour avg: 264m. TrackMan found the gap.
Launch monitor screenshot showing spin rate + carry distance
Before/after swing data comparison

brief.purpose: Drive fitting bookings and coaching sessions by proving Swing Shack's TrackMan technology gives golfers data-driven insight their game has been missing.
brief.audience: Jozi golfers, 25-50, mid-high handicap. They track their fitness — they want to track their golf. Data-aware, skeptical of voodoo tips, willing to pay for evidence-based improvement.
brief.bigIdea: Your swing has a number. TrackMan measures it. That number is the shortcut to better scores.
brief.successMetric: Fitting sessions booked. Secondary: GMB posts live weekly. Tertiary: engagement rate on stat-hook content above 2.5%.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A hook that stops the scroll with a specific number. A visual that shows TrackMan data overlaid on a club or swing. A caption that earns the click by expanding the data story. Booking link front and centre.
brief.whatBadLooksLike: Vague transformation claims ('From confused golfer to confident striker'). Busy backgrounds without contrast. Price-led content without data justification. Anything that looks like generic golf marketing.

dna.tone: Clinical authority. Data speaks, we just translate it. No hype, no fluff — numbers are the argument. Authoritative but not cold. Expert without being gatekeeping.
dna.contentMix: 70% educational (data insights, stats explainers) / 20% promotional (session offers, fitting deals) / 10% social proof (client results, before/after)
forbiddenVisualStyles: text over busy backgrounds without contrast layer
dna.ctaPhilosophy: Direct price-led with anchoring: show the value first (TrackMan data), then introduce the offer. Always include R-amount. 'From R250' works because the data has already justified the price.

platformStrategy.instagram: Stat-first hook stops the scroll. Data overlay on image tells the story. Caption expands with context. Link in bio drives booking.
platformStrategy.tiktok: Hook is the number/stat itself. 'Your drive: 199m' as text overlay. 3-second hook, then explain the data. Fast-cut, punchy.
platformStrategy.gmb: Trust + proof + convenience. Service highlight with one key stat. Clean, professional, no gimmicks. Call to action is always 'book now' or 'call us'.

exampleHighPerforming.whyItWorked: 'Your golf stats don't lie' — specific, implies measurement, triggers curiosity about what the stats reveal. Stats hooks 2.5x better than transformation hooks.

exampleLowPerforming.whyItFailed: 'FROM CONFUSED GOLFER TO CONFIDENT STRIKER' — vague, no data anchor. Transformation claims without proof feel empty.

bestHooks.notes: Stats angle consistently outperforms transformation. 'Your [metric]' format is the winner.

failedContent.reason: Vague transformation claim, no data anchor
failedContent.lesson: Always lead with a number or specific stat. 'Your [X]' outperforms 'FROM [state] TO [state]'
Weather/indoor convenience is table stakes, not a hook. Stats create urgency.

lessonsLearned: Stats hooks consistently outperform all other angles — lead with numbers always
Meters > Yards for SA market — confirmed April 2026
Dark background with data overlay looks premium with TrackMan theme
Caption ≠ Overlay Text — supplementary copy drives click-through, not the hook itself
Hook A best performer (Round 1) was never re-published — opportunity cost

brief.purpose: Establish Takomo 101T as the smart golfer's iron of choice in SA — premium hollow-body technology at a price that challenges the big brands.
brief.audience: Serious golfers, 25-50, mid-to-low handicap. They do their research. They want Tour-level performance without Tour-level prices. They read reviews, compare specs, and buy based on data not branding.
brief.bigIdea: Takomo 101T: the iron that gets serious golfers arguing — and fitting sessions that settle the argument.
brief.successMetric: Takomo fitting sessions booked. Secondary: engagement on Takomo content above TrackMan benchmark. Tertiary: Takomo mentions in bio link clicks.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A real Takomo iron head on pure black — no AI, no stock photos. A price callout in gold that creates urgency without discounting. A hook that poses a question serious golfers want answered. Copy that respects the reader's intelligence.
brief.whatBadLooksLike: AI-generated club heads that look fake. Broken/garbled text. Price claims without the 'under $600' anchor. Generic golf content that could be any iron. Anything that talks down to the audience.

dna.tone: Confident, curious, slightly provocative. The kind of content that makes serious golfers stop and think — then book a fitting to settle the argument. Sharp without being aggressive.
dna.contentMix: 50% product education (what makes Takomo different) / 30% controversy/question angle / 20% value proof (price-to-performance)
preferredVisualStyles: real product photography of Takomo iron head on black
clean product cutout on dark background
gold price callout overlaid on chrome
forbiddenVisualStyles: AI-generated club/product heads (Christelle rule) — real product photography only
busy backgrounds with text overlay without contrast layer
stock golf photos without product context
dna.ctaPhilosophy: Price transparency as hook: lead with 'less than $600' or 'from R250' because the value is the argument. CTAs are always 'Book Takomo Fitting' with R-amount anchored.

platformStrategy.instagram: Product-first: the iron head IS the hero. Price callout in gold. Caption earns the click with the controversy/question angle. Link to booking.
platformStrategy.tiktok: Hook is the price question: 'Is Takomo 101T worth it? We put it on TrackMan.' Product visual first, data second.
platformStrategy.gmb: Takomo fitting service highlight. Price-led. Trust signal: 'Swing Shack is authorized Takomo fitter.'

exampleLowPerforming.whyItFailed: AI-generated club head looked fake. Text broken/garbled. Pricing callout wrong. Product credibility too low. Real product photography required per Christelle gate rule.

failedContent.reason: AI product imagery looks fake. Broken text. Wrong pricing. Product credibility too low.
failedContent.lesson: Golf club/physical product campaigns require real product photography. AI may only do background/layout/text treatment. No AI product heads.

lessonsLearned: For golf clubs and physical products: requiresRealProductImage = true always
AI-generated club heads fail Gate 2 by default
Text must be added as separate design layer — never embedded in generated image
Broken text = automatic quality gate failure

identity.name: Winter Golf
identity.goal: Drive indoor golf sessions during SA winter season

visualDirection.mood: Cozy indoor warmth vs cold outside. Jozi winter contrast. Indoor golf paradise.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Cold outside, warm inside. The contrast between grey Jo'burg winter and the warmth, green satisfaction of indoor golf. Pizzas, beers, premium simulators. Social golf atmosphere. NOT about technique or data — about the experience and enjoyment. Think: pub golf meets luxury simulator.
imageReferences: Simulator screen showing lush course in winter grey context
Cozy indoor setup with warm lighting
Post-round drinks at Swing Shack bar
Rain on window outside, golfer smiling inside
visualDirection.colorUsage: Cool blues for winter theme (#4A90D9). Warm accent for indoor coziness (#D4A574 or warm amber). Never clinical — keep it inviting and social.
visualDirection.typography: Warm, approachable. Bold for contrast headlines. Friendly sans-serif.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split mood: grey/cold outside vs warm/green inside. Social proof. Food and beverage welcome. Not data-heavy.
contentExamples: It's 8°C outside. 22°C inside. Your game never stops.
Rain check? How about a round.
Winter doesn't exist in here.

brief.purpose: Keep Swing Shack bookings steady through SA winter by positioning indoor golf as the obvious choice when outdoor courses go cold.
brief.audience: Regular Jo'burg golfers who stop playing in winter because their home course gets cold or they travel less. They already have clubs — they just need a reason to keep playing.
brief.bigIdea: Winter doesn't exist in here. (It's always 22°C, there's food and drinks, and the simulator never closes.)
brief.successMetric: Winter session bookings vs prior year. Secondary: winter package upsells. Tertiary: social engagement on contrast-style content.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A visual that makes you want to be inside — warm lights, green fairways on screen, something cold and grey outside the window. A hook that names the weather or the day. Content that feels like a friend saying 'actually, this is good.'
brief.whatBadLooksLike: Clinical data overlays. Golf swing technique photos. Anything that makes indoor golf sound like a chore or a substitute. Content that positions winter as a problem rather than Swing Shack as the answer.

dna.tone: Warm, inviting, slightly cheeky. The tone of a friend who knows the best spot in Jo'burg. Not trying to be premium or clinical — just genuinely fun. Think: 'you know what this weather needs? A round.'
dna.contentMix: 40% social proof (look how good it is inside) / 30% contrast/humor (cold vs warm) / 20% practical (sessions available, deals) / 10% lifestyle (food, drinks, atmosphere)
preferredVisualStyles: cozy bar/food setup at Swing Shack
contrast: grey sky outside vs green simulator inside
forbiddenVisualStyles: cold blue colour grading on indoor content
anything that makes indoor golf look like a chore
dna.ctaPhilosophy: Casual and low-friction: 'Book a session' not 'Book now — limited slots.' Make it feel like a no-brainer, not a sales push.

platformStrategy.instagram: Lifestyle-first: food, drinks, simulators, social vibe. Contrast hooks work well. Carousels showing 'inside vs outside' perform.
platformStrategy.tiktok: 'It's [X]°C outside. This is what we did instead.' Fast, relatable, shareable. Show the vibe, not the data.
platformStrategy.gmb: Seasonal/event posts. 'Winter sessions available.' Warm imagery, social proof. 'Book your winter round.'

strategy.positioningStatement: When the courses go cold, the simulator doesn't.
strategy.targetAudience: Regular Jo'burg golfers who play less in winter. They love golf but the weather stops them.
strategy.primaryOffer: Winter sessions from R250. Winter package deals available.

brief.audience: Johannesburg golfers who are using ill-suited clubs, struggling with consistency, or looking to improve their game through better equipment choices.
brief.goalNotes: Drive practice session and fitting bookings by educating golfers on the importance of using the correct clubs for their swing, skill level, and playing style. Reinforce that the right equipment leads to better performance, consistency, and enjoyment on the course.
brief.context: Campaign theme: "You wouldn't dig a hole with a pool noodle. You wouldn't run a marathon in flip-flops. So why play golf with the wrong clubs?" Visual direction should compare obviously incorrect tools or equipment with golfers using unsuitable clubs. Focus on education, performance improvement, and the value of proper club selection and fitting.

strategy.positioningStatement: For Johannesburg golfers who are using ill-suited clubs, struggling with consistency, or looking to improve their game through better equipment choices. who want to Bookings.
strategy.targetAudience: Johannesburg golfers who are using ill-suited clubs, struggling with consistency, or looking to improve their game through better equipment choices.

pillars.name: The Absurdity Principle — making the invisible visible through comparison
pillars.description: Owns the 'recognition' moment — uses obviously wrong equipment comparisons to create an emotional jolt that makes golfers question their own setup. This pillar creates the initial engagement and stops the scroll.

pillars.name: The Swing-Verification Connection — equipment explains performance
pillars.description: Owns the educational bridge — directly connects specific equipment mismatches (shaft flex, club length, lie angle) to common swing problems (slice, topped shots, lack of distance). Converts curiosity into understanding.

pillars.name: The Fitting Reveal — professional validation of the problem
pillars.description: Owns the 'aha moment' credibility — shows the fitting process as diagnostic revelation, not sales pitch. Positions the fitter as an ally uncovering what's been holding the golfer back, not pushing upgrades.

pillars.name: The Transformation Proof — real results from right equipment
pillars.description: Owns social validation — real Johannesburg golfers sharing concrete improvements: "I broke 90 for the first time after my fitting." Must be specific, measurable, relatable to the target audience's aspirations.

pillars.name: The Invitation — removing friction to action
pillars.description: Owns the conversion — direct but not pushy. Presents booking a practice session or fitting as the logical, exciting next step. Removes barriers by being specific about what happens at the session.

dna.tone: Wry, sharp-edged provocation wrapped in warmth — like a friend exposing your blind spot with a knowing grin, then offering the fix
dna.contentMix: 35% absurd comparison / 30% educational connection / 25% transformation proof / 10% direct invitation
preferredVisualStyles: bold typographic overlays on dark backgrounds
dna.ctaPhilosophy: The CTA should feel like the natural, relieved conclusion to a realization — not a sales push. "Book Your Club Audit" or "Get Fitted, Finally" — short, confident, action-oriented.

platformStrategy.instagram: Carousel format works best here: first slide poses the absurd comparison, subsequent slides reveal the golf parallel, final slide presents the solution and CTA. Use Reels for quick-cut comparison montages.
platformStrategy.tiktok: Not specified for this campaign — focus resources on Instagram and GMB where audience intent is higher.
platformStrategy.gmb: Post educational content about club fitting as services, share client testimonials specifically about equipment improvements, use Google Posts to announce fitting promotions and highlight the campaign theme.

visualDirection.mood: Provocative clarity meets confident solution — like a spotlight on a problem you've been ignoring
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should open with the absurd comparison — a handyman about to hammer a nail with a pool noodle, a runner lacing up heels for a marathon. The visual then pivots to a golfer with clearly wrong clubs: a beginner swinging a stiff-shafted blade meant for single-digit handicappers, a powerful player wrestling a ladies-flex graphite shaft. The contrast should be jarring, then the reveal shows the RIGHT clubs in gold, lit dramatically against the dark background — the visual 'aha moment'. Close-up shots of clubface impact, swing motion blur, and fitting session moments create kinetic energy that contrasts with the stillness of the problem.
imageReferences: split-screen: person using garden hose as golf club VS golfer with 10-inch longer than appropriate driver
dramatic low-angle shot of gold-finished iron against black background with steam/mist atmosphere
golfers' confused expression as ball goes drastically offline, shot from behind the target line
close-up fitting session: fitter's hands measuring club length with client watching in background
visualDirection.colorUsage: The near-black background (#0D0D0F) creates a stage for the drama, making the warm orange (#FF6B35) pop with urgency — this is the 'problem' color, the cognitive dissonance. White text provides sharp contrast for immediate readability. Gold (#D4AF37) appears ONLY when presenting the solution — it becomes the visual reward, the promise of correct equipment. This scarcity of gold makes it feel premium and aspirational, not just another color choice.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, condensed sans-serif for headlines — punchy, almost tabloid energy. Clean geometric sans for body text — modern, trustworthy. The contrast between these creates visual tension that mirrors the campaign's argument.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Asymmetric layouts that deliberately off-center key elements — nothing feels 'safe' or comfortable, mirroring the campaign's intent to disrupt. Generous negative space around the problem imagery; tighter composition when presenting the solution.
contentExamples: Carousel: "You wouldn't mow your lawn with scissors. Your buddy swings a stiff-shafted blade meant for scratch players. Same thing."
Reel: Split-screen montage of absurd tools (pool noodle, flip-flops for running, tiny hammer) transitioning to mismatched golf equipment, text overlay reads "Sound ridiculous? This is your 7-iron."
GMB Post: Client testimonial with photo: "I gained 23 yards off the tee after my fitting. Didn't know my clubs were 1.5 inches too long." — includes campaign color scheme

dna.tone: Wry, friendly provocation that makes you smile, nod, and suddenly question everything you thought you knew about your game.
dna.contentMix: 35% provocative comparison content / 30% educational swing science / 20% transformation testimonials / 15% direct CTA and booking prompts
dna.ctaPhilosophy: The CTA should feel like an invitation to join a smarter group, not a sales pitch. 'Book Your Eye-Opening Session' — positioning the booking as discovery, not purchase.

platformStrategy.instagram: Lead with carousel comparisons in feed, use Stories for quick 'Would you?' polls and behind-the-scenes fitting moments, leverage Reels for split-screen swing comparisons with unsuitable vs proper clubs.
platformStrategy.tiktok: N/A for this campaign as per platform selection.
platformStrategy.gmb: Feature educational posts that establish expertise in club fitting, include clear booking CTAs in every post, use the Q&A section to address common equipment misconceptions directly.

exampleHighPerforming: Split-screen video: golfer struggling with 7-iron that bends too much, then seamlessly switching to properly-fitted club with smooth strike
Carousel: 'Would you run a marathon in flip-flops?' → 'So why is your driver 2 degrees too upright?' → CTA to book fitting
exampleLowPerforming: Generic 'Golf equipment on sale' promotional post
Long-form technical blog without visual hooks or emotional trigger

visualDirection.mood: Dramatic revelation under studio lights, like a magician showing the trick behind the illusion.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should open with the absurd comparison — a pool noodle leaning against a sand trap, flip-flops teed up next to a golf ball — then cut to the golfer's face registering the uncomfortable truth. The contrast between ridiculous wrong-tool scenarios and serious golf equipment should feel cinematic and slightly humorous, never preachy. Dark backgrounds make the orange pop with urgency while gold highlights represent the 'aha moment' of discovering the right solution. Every visual should create an instinctive 'wait, that's me' recognition.
imageReferences: Man in full golf attire attempting to chip with a pool noodle, shot in dramatic side lighting against dark background
Split-frame: ill-fitted club bending dramatically at impact vs perfectly matched club compressing the ball cleanly
Close-up of hands gripping wrong vs right shaft, with motion blur on the unsuitable swing
Golfer's face mid-revelation: eyes widening as they watch a comparison demonstration
visualDirection.colorUsage: The dark background (#0D0D0F) creates theatrical drama and makes the warm orange (#FF6B35) impossible to ignore — this urgency color draws the eye to the problem being exposed. White text ensures maximum readability against the darkness. Gold (#D4AF37) appears ONLY at the solution moment, making proper equipment feel earned, premium, and finally correct — the visual reward after the discomfort of recognition.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, condensed sans-serif for headlines to create impact and urgency (think sports editorial), paired with clean geometric body text. Headlines should feel like punchy declarations, not friendly suggestions.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Heavy use of negative space to let the comparison imagery breathe. Strong diagonal lines can suggest motion and the 'wrong' to 'right' journey. The eye should flow naturally from problem (orange) to solution (gold) within each piece.
contentExamples: Carousel post: 'Your driver is lying 2° too upright. Here's what that actually does to your slice.' (Slide 1: problem visualization, Slide 2: swing analysis, Slide 3: booking CTA)
Reel: Side-by-side slow-mo of same golfer hitting cloud of grass with wrong loft vs crisp divot with fitted club. Text overlay: 'The difference isn't in your swing.'
GMB Q&A: 'My friend said fitted clubs are a gimmick. Is that true?' — Answer with specific data point about distance loss from improper shaft flex.
Story poll: 'Would you use a tennis racket to play golf?' with results showing obvious 'no', followed by 'So why is your 5-wood acting like one?'

pillars.name: The Absurdity Mirror — exposing unconscious equipment contradictions
pillars.description: Owns the provocative hook that makes people stop scrolling. Uses obviously ridiculous comparisons (pool noodle, flip-flops) to reflect the absurdity of playing with clubs that fight your swing rather than complement it. Creates the initial recognition without judgment.

pillars.name: Swing Mechanics Decoded — why wrong clubs sabotage specific movements
pillars.description: Owns the educational proof layer. Explains concrete cause-and-effect: how wrong shaft flex creates errant fades, incorrect lie angles cause slices, mismatched clubhead speed compounds inconsistent contact. Makes the invisible problem visible through specific mechanics.

pillars.name: The Fitting Revelation — what proper equipment actually feels like
pillars.description: Owns the transformation promise and sensory experience. Describes what properly fitted clubs feel like at impact — the 'forgiving compression', the effortless height, the confidence at address. Positions fitting not as expense but as finally playing on an even keel.

pillars.name: Local Proof Points — Johannesburg golfer transformations
pillars.description: Owns social validation through relatable local examples. Showcases Johannesburg golfers who experienced the 'before' confusion and the 'after' clarity. Specific handicap improvements, distance gains, consistency breakthroughs — makes the abstract benefit concrete and achievable.

pillars.name: The Booking Bridge — turning awareness into action
pillars.description: Owns the conversion moment and removes friction. Answers the unspoken objection ('Is this really for me?') and guides toward booking a practice session or fitting. Positions the session as the first step in understanding, not a commitment to purchase.

visualDirection.mood: Midnight revelation meets driving range intensity — dramatic, eye-opening, premium.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should feature dramatic side-by-side or split-screen comparisons where one half shows an obviously ridiculous scenario (person trying to dig a foundation with a garden fork, running a sprint in heels) and the other half shows a golfer with clearly wrong equipment — too long clubs, wrong flex, mismatched set. The contrast should feel slightly comedic at first, then land with uncomfortable recognition. Dark, moody lighting on golf equipment shots to create premium feel. The 'solution' moments — clubs being properly fitted, proper address positions — should be bathed in gold accent lighting to signal the 'right choice' revelation.

dramatic overhead shot of mismatched golf clubs scattered on a fitting mat with dark moody background lighting
gold-accented close-up of precise club fitting moment with calliper measurement equipment visible
comparison of same golfer swing with wrong clubs (awkward, inconsistent) VS correctly fitted clubs (smooth, confident)
visualDirection.colorUsage: The dark background (#0D0D0F) creates theatre — making the comparison scenarios pop dramatically and lending gravitas to the equipment conversation. Orange (#FF6B35) functions as the 'wake-up' signal, used sparingly on key provocation text and comparison highlights to create urgency without feeling cheap. Gold (#D4AF37) is reserved exclusively for the solution moments — fitting results, correct equipment, the 'after' state — creating an aspirational contrast that makes the right choice feel premium and worth pursuing.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, condensed sans-serif for headline statements that pose the comparison questions — these need to land with impact and readability at small sizes. Clean, modern sans-serif for body text that maintains sophistication. The contrast between punchy headlines and refined body copy mirrors the campaign's core argument: obvious absurdity meets expert guidance.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Asymmetric layouts that visually represent the 'wrong vs right' tension work best — offset elements, intentional white space on one side, bold placement on the other. Carousel layouts should build tension slide by slide, with the question posed on slide one and the answer revealed progressively. Avoid centered, balanced layouts — the imbalance mirrors the equipment mismatch the campaign critiques.

visualDirection.mood: Sharp, confrontational clarity with a satisfying reveal.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should create visceral discomfort before relief. Open with images that feel WRONG—a chef trying to flip pancakes with a putter, a surgeon reaching for a 3-iron instead of a scalpel, a golfer slicing with clubs clearly too long for their frame. Then pivot hard to the gold-accented solution moment: a perfectly struck iron, a fitted club in hand, a golfer's face showing genuine confidence. The contrast must be immediate and undeniable. Dark backgrounds make the orange urgency pop and the gold solution glow like a beacon. Avoid subtlety—every visual should communicate 'this is obviously wrong, and the fix is obvious too.'

visualDirection.colorUsage: The deep black background (#0D0D0F) creates theatrical darkness that makes every element feel intentional and dramatic—it's the stage for the 'obvious wrongness' reveal. Warm orange (#FF6B35) functions as a warning signal, the visual equivalent of saying 'stop, look at this'—it should appear on the absurd comparisons and problem indicators. Gold (#D4AF37) ONLY appears at the moment of solution, making it feel like the earned reward after acknowledging the problem. White text ensures legibility against the dark backdrop while maintaining the stark, high-contrast aesthetic.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, sans-serif type with heavy weight for headlines—think condensed athletic fonts or industrial stencil styles that feel direct and unapologetic. Body text should be clean and readable, contrasting with the aggressive headlines to guide the eye from problem to solution.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split compositions that force comparison are essential—visuals should literally show wrong vs. right, before vs. after, without requiring mental effort from the viewer. Generous negative space around key messages prevents visual clutter and maintains the sharp, editorial feel.

pillars.name: The Swing Truth — data-driven discomfort
pillars.description: Owns the educational credibility. Delivers concrete evidence that wrong equipment creates swing compensations—loss of distance, inconsistency, higher scores. Uses before/after data, swing plane analysis, and ball flight comparisons to make the problem measurable and undeniable.

pillars.name: The Johannesburg Proof — local transformation stories
pillars.description: Owns social proof and relatability. Features real Johannesburg golfers (handicap badges, local course references) who experienced dramatic improvement after fitting. Their stories validate the campaign's core argument through lived experience rather than abstract claims.

pillars.name: The Fitting Reveal — showing the solution
pillars.description: Owns the transformation process. Demystifies club fitting by showing what happens during a session—launch monitor data, shaft options, lie angle adjustments. Makes the booking decision feel informed rather than risky by demonstrating exactly what the golfer gains.

pillars.name: The Right Club Payoff — celebrating the fix
pillars.description: Owns the emotional reward. Shows the moment a golfer hits a pure shot with properly fitted clubs—the feel, the flight, the confidence. This pillar delivers the satisfaction payoff that makes the entire campaign arc feel complete and worth acting on.

visualDirection.mood: Dark, cinematic theatre of the absurd — one moment you're laughing at a ridiculous comparison, the next you're staring at your own golf bag with new suspicion.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Every visual opens with an obviously wrong equipment scenario — a shovel bent in half, a chef trying to chop with a fork, a swimmer in a suit of armour — then cuts to a golfer experiencing an equivalent equipment mismatch. The golfer should look frustrated, confused, almost defeated. The reveal moment shows the same golfer with properly fitted clubs, and the contrast is lit in gold: the gold accent only appears when the RIGHT equipment enters the frame. Dark backgrounds make the warm orange urgency pop; the gold solution glows against the black like a light going on. No clutter — every frame holds one powerful idea.
imageReferences: A golfer gripping a driver that is visibly too long for their stature, shadow stretching wildly off-axis, dark studio background with single rim light
Split-screen: left side shows a hand gripping a pool noodle as if it's a putter; right side shows a golfer gripping a putter that is clearly the wrong lie angle — both in the same frustrated pose
A close-up of a clubface at address, perfectly centred, but the shaft is bowed incorrectly — lit dramatically in dark background with gold accent light catching the clubhead only
visualDirection.colorUsage: The #0D0D0F near-black background creates dramatic tension and forces the eye to the warm orange #FF6B35 which signals urgency and the problem. White #FFFFFF text remains clean and readable against dark. The gold #D4AF37 accent is reserved exclusively for the 'solution moment' — when fitted clubs appear, when the booking CTA is shown, when the golfer smiles — so the colour becomes synonymous with relief and the right answer. This gradient from dark to orange to gold mirrors the emotional journey from problem recognition to resolution.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, condensed sans-serif for headline comparisons — short, punchy, almost aggressive in scale. Clean medium-weight sans-serif for body copy and educational content. Never italic, never decorative. The contrast between the bold absurd headlines and the calm explanatory body copy mirrors the campaign's rhetorical structure: provoke first, explain second.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Single-focus layouts only. One absurdity per frame. Generous negative space on dark backgrounds so the warm orange and gold elements command attention without competition. Never centre-aligned text blocks — left-align with intentional asymmetry to feel editorial and purposeful, not corporate. Use full-bleed dark backgrounds on Instagram feed posts; Stories can use the orange as a top or bottom bar accent.
contentExamples: Reel: 'Would you fix a car with a spoon? So why are you playing with clubs that don't fit?' — 12-second hook, cut to fitted club reveal, CTA overlay
Carousel: 'The Pool Noodle Test: 3 swings your wrong clubs are stealing from you' — educational slides, booking CTA on final slide
Story: Poll asking 'Which is worse — wrong shoes or wrong clubs?' with real-time results and a follow-up message revealing the data on how ill-fitted clubs affect Johannesburg golfers' scores
GMB pinned post: 'Still playing with last season's hand-me-downs? Here's why your swing deserves better equipment — and how a 30-minute practice session can prove it.'

pillars.name: The Absurdity Principle — Make the Wrong Obvious
pillars.description: This pillar owns the provocation angle. Every piece of content opens by confronting the golfer with an undeniable absurdity — using the wrong tool for the job — and drawing a direct, uncomfortable parallel to their club choice. Without this hook, there is no engagement. It drives initial stop-scroll and awareness by making the audience feel seen and slightly foolish in a way that creates curiosity, not defensiveness.

pillars.name: Swing Faults Aren't Skill Problems — They're Equipment Problems
pillars.description: This pillar owns the education layer. It takes common golfer frustrations (inconsistency, slices, lack of distance, topped shots) and reframes them not as skill deficiencies but as symptoms of wrong equipment. Content under this pillar shows specific swing faults linked to specific club mismatches — wrong shaft flex, incorrect lie angle, improper shaft length — so the golfer begins to diagnose their own bag through this new lens.

pillars.name: Fitting Is Discovery, Not Shopping
pillars.description: This pillar owns the positioning of club fitting as a transformative experience, not a retail transaction. It shifts the perception from 'I need new clubs' to 'I need to understand what's been holding my game back.' This pillar builds desire for the practice session by framing the booking as the beginning of a discovery journey — a 30-minute session that reveals something fundamental about the golfer's game they didn't know.

pillars.name: Johannesburg Course Confidence — The Local Reality
pillars.description: This pillar owns geographic and social proof for the Johannesburg audience. It grounds the campaign in local context — specific Johannesburg course conditions, altitude affecting ball flight, the pressure of playing with members who have fitted clubs — making the campaign feel relevant, local, and urgent. This pillar converts the general awareness from pillars 1-3 into a Johannesburg-specific reason to act now.

pillars.name: The Right Equipment Reveal — Gold Moment Booking
pillars.description: This pillar owns the conversion moment. Every content piece ends here — the gold-accented reveal where fitted clubs and a confident golfer appear, and the CTA to book a practice session becomes impossible to ignore. This pillar is the emotional payoff of the entire campaign: the moment the audience thinks 'Okay, I get it. I need to do this.' It converts awareness into action through a single, specific, frictionless booking ask.

Strategic goal: position fitting as accessible science, not intimidating mystery.

pillars.name: The Transformation Proof — Johannesburg golfer fitting success stories

pillars.name: The Easy Next Step — removing friction to book a practice and fitting session

Direct booking CTAs with clear value proposition. Strategic goal: convert awareness into action by making 'book now' feel like the obvious, easy choice.

visualDirection.typography: Bold, condensed sans-serif for headlines — punchy, almost tabloid energy. Clean geometric sans for body text — modern, trustworthy. The contrast between these creates visual tension that mirrors the campaign's argument.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Asymmetric layouts that deliberately off-center key elements — nothing feels 'safe' or comfortable, mirroring the campaign's intent to disrupt. Generous negative space around the problem imagery; tighter composition when presenting the solution.
contentExamples: Carousel: "You wouldn't mow your lawn with scissors. Your buddy swings a stiff-shafted blade meant for scratch players. Same thing."
Reel: Split-screen montage of absurd tools (pool noodle, flip-flops for running, tiny hammer) transitioning to mismatched golf equipment, text overlay reads "Sound ridiculous? This is your 7-iron."
GMB Post: Client testimonial with photo: "I gained 23 yards off the tee after my fitting. Didn't know my clubs were 1.5 inches too long." — includes campaign color scheme

pillars.name: The Absurdity Principle — making the invisible visible through comparison
pillars.description: Owns the 'recognition' moment — uses obviously wrong equipment comparisons to create an emotional jolt that makes golfers question their own setup. This pillar creates the initial engagement and stops the scroll.

pillars.name: The Swing-Verification Connection — equipment explains performance
pillars.description: Owns the educational bridge — directly connects specific equipment mismatches (shaft flex, club length, lie angle) to common swing problems (slice, topped shots, lack of distance). Converts curiosity into understanding.

pillars.name: The Fitting Reveal — professional validation of the problem
pillars.description: Owns the 'aha moment' credibility — shows the fitting process as diagnostic revelation, not sales pitch. Positions the fitter as an ally uncovering what's been holding the golfer back, not pushing upgrades.

pillars.name: The Transformation Proof — real results from right equipment
pillars.description: Owns social validation — real Johannesburg golfers sharing concrete improvements: "I broke 90 for the first time after my fitting." Must be specific, measurable, relatable to the target audience's aspirations.

pillars.name: The Invitation — removing friction to action
pillars.description: Owns the conversion — direct but not pushy. Presents booking a practice session or fitting as the logical, exciting next step. Removes barriers by being specific about what happens at the session.
